findings.reason: The protected query is the canonical expert-interview self-join solution. Descriptive point aliases, one strict ID comparison, two explicit non-degeneracy filters, the direct area formula, and the complete three-key ordering make the data flow immediately recognizable without redundant grouping or deduplication. No material improvement warrants an inert candidate.

For every two distinct point IDs, exactly one orientation satisfies first_point.id < second_point.id, so every unordered pair is considered once with p1 < p2. Unequal x- and y-coordinates are respectively equivalent to positive width and height; their absolute differences therefore multiply to the exact positive area. Conversely, every valid axis-aligned rectangle formed from two rows satisfies those predicates and is emitted once. The explicit descending area and ascending ID keys establish the complete output order.

The self-join considers O(P^2) unordered point pairs and emits R at most P(P - 1) / 2 rows. Constant work computes each area, and sorting R outputs costs O(R log R), giving the declared O(P^2 log P) worst-case time and O(R) sort materialization space. The complexity artifact is inherited, hash-bound identity only; this accelerated review did not inspect or recalibrate it and did not claim a fresh runtime verdict.

The query preserves unique point IDs, integer coordinates, the axis-aligned opposite-corner interpretation, non-zero area, p1 and p2 projection, and every ordering tie-breaker. It correctly excludes pairs sharing either coordinate and handles signed coordinates through ABS without depending on input order or consecutive IDs.

The complete Approach accurately targets the unchanged query and explains single-orientation pair generation, coordinate filters, absolute-difference area, deterministic ordering, completeness, and the O(P^2 log P) and O(R) bounds. Its alternatives and edge cases cover duplicate pair generation, unnecessary rescans, zero dimensions, duplicate coordinates, negative values, sparse IDs, tied areas, and insufficient rows.

The protected app-local and immutable native SQL files are byte-identical and remain unchanged at canonical SHA-256 c1e9702903cd45db138e44d9ffb94d94279d75dfe38a6f921ff8ffaff22897c0. They use the same self-join, filters, projection, area expression, and ordering, while verified submission 2069173889 remains untouched.

Authenticated Premium evidence confirmed the three-column Points schema, axis-aligned non-zero-area requirement, p1/p2/area definitions, complete descending-and-ascending ordering rules, one exact explained example, and one source diagram. The modular Reference preserves the three source tables and replaces the provider image with an independently authored accessible pair-evaluation table that captures every point, width, height, area, valid rectangle, and zero-area exclusion. It is bound to live content SHA-256 566530599892c299eaafe64ed1ff4ec2280edfa8da31c4584ff85d9e5ca99442.
